fields.name: attack
fields.description: Attack = ramp up, Decay = drop to sustain level, Sustain = plateau, release = ramp off.  Image search for ADSR envelope online for a visual representation of the attack,decay,sustain,release curve. Attack is the ramp up of camera shake (time in seconds).

fields.name: decay
fields.description: Attack = ramp up, Decay = drop to sustain level, Sustain = plateau, release = ramp off.  Image search for ADSR envelope online for a visual representation of the attack,decay,sustain,release curve.  Decay is the drop from the attack height to the sustain height (time in seconds).

fields.name: fall_off_distance
fields.description: Distance, in metres, from the camera shake position, that the camera shake drops to zero.

fields.name: horizontal_amplitude
fields.description: Horizontal movement amplitude of the camera

fields.name: horizontal_frequency
fields.description: Horizontal movement frequency of the camera

fields.name: octave_amplitude_multiplier
fields.description: This is an overall master controller for the amplitude of the noise used in the camera shake.   This is a multiplier which is applied to all of the amplitude controls in the table.

fields.name: octave_frequency_multiplier
fields.description: This is an overall master controller for the frequency of the noise used in the camera shake.    This is a multiplier which is applied to all of the frequency controls in the table.

fields.name: octaves
fields.description: Octaves controls the levels of noise applied to the camera shake.   Each layer is higher in frequency and with less amplitude than the previous layer.   Each new layer will add more expense to the setup.

fields.name: pitch_amplitude
fields.description: Rotation amplitude around the horizontal axis of the camera.  Image search for 'roll pitch yaw' for a diagram.

fields.name: pitch_frequency
fields.description: Rotation frequency around the horizontal axis of the camera.  Image search for 'roll pitch yaw' for a diagram.

fields.name: release
fields.description: Attack = ramp up, Decay = drop to sustain level, Sustain = plateau, release = ramp off. Image search for ADSR envelope online for a visual representation of the attack,decay,sustain,release curve.  Release is the ramp off of camera shake (time in seconds).

fields.name: roll_amplitude
fields.description: Rotation amplitude around the axis the camera is pointing in.   Image search for 'roll pitch yaw' for a diagram.

fields.name: roll_frequency
fields.description: Rotation frequency around the axis the camera is pointing in.  Image search for 'roll pitch yaw' for a diagram.

fields.name: sustain
fields.description: Attack = ramp up, Decay = drop to sustain level, Sustain = plateau, release = ramp off. Image search for ADSR envelopse online for a visual representation of the curve. Sustain is the plateau of camera shake (time in seconds).

fields.name: sustain_multiplier
fields.description: The sustain multiplier is a proportion of the maximum attack value on the curve.   So, if the maximum attack value reaches 2.5 and the sustain multiplier is 0.5, then the sustain value is 1.25.  Image search for ADSR envelope online for a visual representation of the attack,decay,sustain,release curve.

The actual amount is as follows: An intermediary value is formed as max(CAI variable max_goal_evalautions_per_faction, CAI variable max_goal_evalautions_per_round / alive non-rebel factions). assume_failure_score;;;;;(real) If an item's score while performing analysis is ever less than this value, we skip performing later queries. This acts as an optimization so that queries intended as strict filters can be run first, leaving more detailed analysis and queries to only be performed if they fail. The default value is -9.9 so that a negative score of -10 ensures failure (epsilon of 0.1 for potential float inaccuracy).:::::normalize_scores;;;;;(boolean) Whether we should normalize scores before selection. This occurs after score_threshold_min, but before treat_score_as_probability has taken place. agent_subtype;;;;;(agent_subtypes key) Used by agent subtype checking queries to determine what type we are checking:::::allow_land_sea_transition;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not we can cross from land to sea regions in our search:::::building_set;;;;;(building_set key) Used by ERS type checking queries if the slot is associated with a specific building set record:::::decision_item;;;;;(cai_decision_items key) Used by history checking queries to define what decision item we are checking. If this is null, then it defaults to the current decision item being analyzed.:::::decision_profile;;;;;(cai_decision_profiles key) Used by history checking queries to define what decision profile we are checking. If this is null, then it defaults to the current decision profile performing analysis.:::::default_query_result;;;;;(real) The default value a query will return when in an invalid state (for example missing contextual information). Database table information in scoring (e.g query_invert_result, query_weight) will still be applied to this value. However, other query variables are ignored: for example, queries that utilize min_max_behaviour will return the default_query_result directly, instead of passing it through the min_max_behaviour.:::::ers_construction_state;;;;;("empty", "constructing", "finished", "sacked", "ruined", "attackable") Used by ERS state checking queries to determine ERS_CONSTRUCTION_STATE. Returns 1 for a match, 0 otherwise. "attackable" is a match for both "constructing" and "finished":::::force_stance;;;;;(campaign_stances key) Used by stance checking queries to determine what stance we are checking or filtering by:::::force_type;;;;;(military_force_types key) Used by military force type checking queries to determine what type we are checking or filtering by:::::history_specificity;;;;;("any", "target", "target_or_third_party", "target_and_third_party") Used to define the level of specificity for the decision_item history queries. "any" checks for a decision against any target/third_party, "target" looks for a decision against the same target, "target_or_third_party" looks for a decision where either the target or the third party were involved. "target_and_third_party" is a directional equivilant of target_or_third_party: target_or_third_party doesn't differentiate between the target/third_party while target_and_third_party does. The former is useful for non-directional questions ("did I force faction a and b to go to war?") while the latter is useful for more directional ones ("did I force faction a to raid faction b?"):::::ignore_abandoned_regions;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not to ignore abandoned regions:::::ignore_armed_citizenry;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not to ignore armed citizenry (i.e garrisons):::::ignore_rebels;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not to ignore rebel regions/forces:::::max;;;;;(real) Generic max; see min_max_behaviour:::::max_random_extension;;;;;(real) Used to add randomness in min/max: When the max variable is used, a random number between 0 and this value will be added onto the max.:::::min;;;;;(real) Generic min; see min_max_behaviour:::::min_max_behaviour;;;;;("bounds", "bounds_exclusive", "scaled", "none") If "bounds", then the check types will return 1 if the checked value is between min and max inclusive. This is useful for "has at least X money" or "has less then X public order" type checks. "bounds_exclusive" is the same, but checks exclusive instead of inclusive. If "scaled", then the check types will return 0 if the checked value is below min, 1 if the checked value is above max, and linearly interpolate in-between. If "none", then we return the underlying value of the query without modification.:::::min_random_extension;;;;;(real) Used to add randomness in min/max: When the min variable is used, a random number between 0 and this value will be added onto the min. Please ensure that min + min_random_extension is not greater than max!:::::owned_by;;;;;("self", "self_or_allied", "only_allied", "neutral", "enemy", "any") Used by searching queries to determine the owner of regions/military force in the query. This is relative to the domain; i.e, if domain is an enemy, then "owned_by: self" means the enemy owns that thing, not the analysing faction! This also only includes known factions; even "any" here will only check known factions.:::::pooled_resource;;;;;(pooled_resources key) Used by pooled resource checking queries to determine what pooled resource we are checking the value of.:::::queried_domain;;;;;("source, "target", "third_party", "most_specific") In many cases, an object may be making an decision regarding something other than itself. This variable allows defining whether we are checking something about the object making a decision (source), the object being acted upon (target), or a tertiary involved object that may be required for targeting (third_party). Most specific chooses third_party if it's set, otherwise target, and finally otherwise source.:::::queried_domain_2;;;;;("source, "target", "third_party", "most_specific") "x_to_x" queries do comparisons, and this domain acts as a secondary argument of the other thing to compare against.:::::region;;;;;(region key) Used by region checking queries to determine what campaign region we are checking:::::region_group;;;;;(region_groups key) Used by region group checking queries to determine what campaign region group we are checking:::::region_hint;;;;;(cai_region_hints key) Used by region checking queries if the region is marked by a specific region hint:::::region_lost_recently_time_horizon;;;;;(cardinal) Used by faction_to_region_check_if_lost_region_recently query to determine how many rounds back we check. Note, this is as yet limited to a max of 10!:::::region_range;;;;;(cardinal) Used by searching queries to determine how many regions outwards to search. 0: this region, 1: this region and surrounding regions, etc.:::::shared_state;;;;;(string) Used by shared state checking queries to determine what shared state key value we are checking.:::::subculture;;;;;(cultures_subcultures key) Used by queries that check what subculture a faction uses
